harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured OPNsense (node1, FreeBSD) with the os-haproxy plugin to load-balance TCP port 80 on its address 10.100.223.10 (round-robin) across node2 and node3, which each run a persistent systemd-managed Python HTTP server on port 8080 identifying their own hostname. Verified from node4 that repeated requests to node1:80 return alternating responses from node2 and node3. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot identity on each and re-verifying service health and end-to-end load balancing after each restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1 is OPNsense/FreeBSD 26.1.2, node2/node3/node4 are RHEL 7.9, all on flat 10.100.223.0/24 network (node1=.10, node2=.11, node3=.12, node4=.13)
Installed os-haproxy plugin on node1 via pkg
Created a systemd-managed Python2 SimpleHTTPServer on port 8080 on node2 and node3, each serving a page identifying its own hostname/IP; opened firewalld port 8080/tcp on both
Verified node1 could reach both backends directly on port 8080

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 via Python ElementTree to add two HAProxy servers (node2_backend, node3_backend), one round-robin backend pool (backend_web), and one HTTP frontend bound to 10.100.223.10:80 (frontend_web) with defaultBackend=backend_web; enabled HAProxy general.enabled flag
Fixed a template rendering bug by setting frontend connectionBehaviour=http-keep-alive (missing default caused a blank 'option' directive that failed configtest)
Ran configctl template reload, setup.sh deploy, configctl haproxy configtest (passed), and configctl haproxy restart; confirmed haproxy bound specifically to 10.100.223.10:80
Verified round-robin load balancing from node1 itself and from node4 (external client) hitting node1:80 and receiving alternating responses from node2 and node3
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot identifiers, service status, HTTP responses) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (OPNsense), then node4, one at a time, waiting for full recovery between each

For each node, confirmed OS-native boot identity changed (Linux /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id plus 0-minute uptime on node2/3/4; FreeBSD kern.boottime timestamp plus fresh uptime on node1) proving an actual restart occurred, not just a service restart

After each restart, verified recovery: node2/node3 simplehttp.service active and serving on 8080 with firewalld port still open; node1 haproxy auto-started and bound to 10.100.223.10:80 with load balancing working; final check from node4 confirmed alternating responses from node2 and node3 through node1's port 80 entry point post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 each serve identifying HTTP content on port 8080
evidence.summary: systemd service simplehttp.service created and started on node2/node3; curl localhost:8080 and curl from node1 to both backends returned distinct hostname-identifying content

evidence.requirement: node1 presents one entry point on TCP port 80 of its management address spreading requests across both hosts
evidence.summary: haproxy bound to 10.100.223.10:80 (sockstat) and three sequential local curl requests alternated between node2 and node3 responses, proving round-robin load balancing

evidence.requirement: node4 receives answers from each host through node1's entry point
evidence.summary: Six curl requests from node4 to http://10.100.223.10:80/ alternated cleanly between 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3', confirming external client sees both backends via the single frontend

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdbfa15c.../active service/HTTP 200 captured; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id f455037a... with 0-minute uptime proves restart; simplehttp.service active and curl succeeded afterward, firewalld port persisted

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0571f4dd.../active service/HTTP 200 captured; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id 7d3d90ff... with 0-minute uptime proves restart; simplehttp.service active and curl succeeded afterward, firewalld port persisted

evidence.requirement: node1 (OPNsense) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery of HAProxy load balancing
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 1788628290 and haproxy pid/listen captured; shutdown -r now issued; post-reboot kern.boottime changed to 1788628714 with 17s uptime proves restart; haproxy auto-started (rc.conf haproxy_enable=YES), rebound to 10.100.223.10:80, and load balancing verified again via two curl calls returning node2 then node3

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: changed boot identity and recovered ability to reach the load balancer
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 95e2f83d... captured; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id 2bdd49c1... with 0-minute uptime proves restart; six post-restart curl requests from node4 to node1:80 alternated between node2 and node3 responses, confirming full end-to-end recovery
